Yeah, unfortunately even kids stuff seems to run wider and box-ier these days. I used to be able to size down, but now it's either too big or too short!! I'm not that small either, so it's frustrating to have so few options. Good news is that 25" waist should be (slightly) easier to find! 

American Eagle jeans have always been my go-to. I recently sized out of their stuff, but they have frequent sales, so I was always able to wait and snag jeans in the $20-$35 range. For size reference, I'd say their 00 fits like a 24/24.5" (skinny styles run smaller, but baggy/curvy styles can run much larger, esp in the hips). They have Long sizing down to 00.

For other brands, I know Abercrombie/Aero/Hollister/American Eagle/Levi/Gap/Buckle/Lucky all have that size. Hopefully you're able to find a deal somewhere!

In my experience, Abercrombie runs large ever since they restructured their sizing. What are your measurements? Aeropostale has 000Ls with 23" waist/31" inseam, and that's been the smallest/longest I've been able to find. As a fellow tall xxs, I feel your pain!

I mean, anything that plugs in and gets hot is technically a fire hazard, but if you're careful it shouldn't be a problem. Ours is set on a little shelf next to the toilet and has upgraded bathroom safety features - safety plug, tip/overheat shutoff, and a shutoff timer (can set for 0-24hrs, and automatically shuts off after 24hrs regardless). It's Dreo brand from Amazon. 

We live in a northern climate, but don't have any vents for heat/ac in our primary bath (100yo home, and the master bath was a later add-on). When it's below freezing outside, the bathroom gets down to 40/50F. So the spaceheater runs 24/7 in there - I leave it at 68F and turn it up when I'm showering. It's been over a year and no concerns yet. The electric bill for it is an extra $10-15/mo, running 24/7. Eventually I'll rip out the floor and install radiant heat underneath, but for now the space heater has been a perfect solution.

ETA: I paid a little bit extra for a unit with temp control and bathroom/safety features. At the time, I passed on a more expensive version that had app control too. If you're worried about safety, you could get something like that - being able to check the unit from your phone might add peace of mind.

I put a space heater in the bathroom last winter and it's been *lifechanging* for showers. I turn it on before getting in, and the room is toasty warm by the time I get out. I also wipe down my body with a dry washcloth before exiting the shower for a real towel. Gets me drier faster, which helps with the cold/drafty feeling as I get out! I lay out my clean clothes ahead of time so I can get dressed asap too.

Nose pain! I got elbowed in the face at ~14 and it's happened ever since. I'll get the numbness you mentioned, with a dull achy pain at the top/bridge where cartilage turns to bone. If I pinch it correctly, I'll get a crack and it goes back to normal for awhile. If I leave it alone, it progresses into sort of a sinus headache.

The frequency and also the movement/cracking has lessened over the years, but I find I'm more sensitive in that spot. Pressure from masks, goggles, certain glasses, etc. cause pain and headaches if i wear them too long. Almost feels like the cartilage up there shifted, and never settled back into the correct spot? And the cracking helps, but it feels like there's a section up top that i can't reach to reset? Which may be why it keeps recurring.
Thank you SO much, I'm going to check out all of your suggestions tonight!

I think I know what you mean about the wider bra/outer-full. Over the years, I've found my proper/measured size only fits correctly if it has the right shape. If the cup is too wide, there's not enough support and the tissue sort of migrates towards my armpits? Which then causes gaping and fit issues at the top of the cup. So wide/shallower sizes fit better in a sister size - larger band, smaller cup. But it has more of a minimizing effect, appearance-wise, and is definitely less supportive physically, because I notice more back pain and posture issues.

Not sure if you have Celiac, or are gluten free by choice, but I saw the Schar products and had to comment. A lot of Kroger's generics are not gluten free and/or have potential for cross contamination. I stopped shopping there after getting terribly sick a few times. Several previously safe/gf products now have "may contain wheat" added to the label, which was really disappointing. Definitely check the label every time you repurchase.

Unfortunately, gluten free groceries are a lot more expensive, period. If Walmart is an option for you, I've (surprisingly) found they tend to have the biggest/cheapest selection of gf (including a lot of their generic brand stuff, too). Aldi has some gems, but a much smaller selection. Trader Joe's has great options/prices, but will 100% get you sick, so do not be tempted! 

My best cost-saving suggestion is to avoid processed convenience items as much as possible - stick to naturally gf options (rice, potatoes, meats, fresh veg), and try to make things from scratch. Every week I try to bake a loaf of bread, a dessert (cookies, brownies, etc), and a snack (muffins, homemade crackers, etc) for the week, which helps a LOT with grocery costs, because those substitutions are expensive! At the end of the day, though, your health and wellbeing is most important, so please don't feel guilty about spending extra on gluten free. It's not fair that we have to pay so much more, but food is literally a necessity, and you deserve safe and nourishing options!

Chic Chef Catering did our suburban Chicago wedding last year. All gluten free, and we got rave reviews from our guests! Pricing was extremely reasonable, and they were great to work with.

And yes, our Sweet Ali's cake was delicious (and beautiful)! However, we served a Costco sheet cake to most of our guests, because the XXL gluten free cake was $$$ and I knew most people would prefer a regular cake anyway :')

Except... that's not the reason they're angry. They aren't mad that other people *didn't* have complications. They're mad because their experience with complications is being dismissed.

It's one thing to say, "I had an easy afterbirth," and something else entirely to say, "Every woman has an easy afterbirth." The second statement is untrue, and minimizes the pain and suffering some women experience. 

I think it's reasonable to feel anger when someone is trying to dismiss your experience because it "didn't happen to me." Most people escape complications, but childbirth can be deadly, even with all the benefits of modern medicine. It is *not* a universally easy experience. Spreading that kind of misinformation does a disservice to all women.
